solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Place American flag with difficulty (8)

blocks.note: a regiment's flag is its colours; the American spelling drops the U
ado = fuss, trouble, as in 'without further ado'

annotation.surface: Someone plants the Stars and Stripes somewhere, and it takes some effort.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American' looks like part of the flag-planting picture, but its real job is to tell you to use the US spelling.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this US state is one of countless places, and the vague word hides that a proper name is wanted.

entries.clue: Standing, quietly released gas? Run away! (6)

indicatorNotes.Standing: in a down clue, a word stood upright is read from the bottom up, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: to mace someone is to spray them with Mace, a disabling gas

annotation.surface: Someone upright quietly breaks wind, and the others are told to flee.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a schoolboy joke about wind; the gas is actually Mace, the spray. The whole string P + MACED is then stood on its head.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to break camp and slip off, as an army or a lodger might, is to run away.

entries.clue: Bible is definite covering reported tomb? (9)

indicatorNotes.covering: a cover goes over and around what it covers, so the outer word wraps the inner one
indicatorNotes.reported: what is reported reaches us by ear, so only the sound of the word counts

blocks.note: sure = certain, definite; it goes outside
a crypt is an underground tomb; by sound it can be spelt CRIPT

annotation.surface: A question whether the Bible settles something about a tomb spoken of, perhaps Christ's.
annotation.walkthrough: CRIPT is not a word, only a spelling of the sound of CRYPT, which is why the homophone is needed before the container can close.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the Bible is the holy writ of Christianity, and 'the Scriptures' is its standard alternative name.

entries.clue: America consumed by rapid criticism (7)

indicatorNotes.consumed by: food consumed by someone ends up inside them, so the first piece goes inside the second

blocks.note: flying = very fast, as in a flying start

annotation.surface: The United States gets swallowed up by fast-moving criticism.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rapid criticism' reads as one phrase; split it after 'rapid'.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: to strip the skin off someone is a metaphor for savage verbal attack, so the noun names harsh criticism.

entries.clue: A large piece turned in wood (5)

indicatorNotes.turned: something turned round faces the other way, so its letters read backwards

blocks.note: the A stays as it is
a slab is a large thick piece

annotation.surface: A woodturner makes a big piece on the lathe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned in wood' reads as lathe work, but 'in' only links the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this very light tropical timber, loved by model-makers, is one kind of wood.

entries.clue: Domestic charge paid in advance (8)

blocks.note: a domestic is a household servant, a noun here
a fee paid up front to keep a lawyer or adviser on call

annotation.surface: A household bill paid before it falls due.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' looks like an adjective describing the charge; it is a noun, a servant, as in an old family retainer.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a servant retained by a household for years, and the fee that retains a professional's services.

entries.clue: Stroke of genius finally after sweats? (6)

indicatorNotes.finally: what comes finally comes at the very end, so take the word's last letter
indicatorNotes.after: a thing placed after another follows it, so this letter goes on the end

blocks.note: to sweat over something is to worry, to fret

annotation.surface: A brilliant idea arrives at last after much perspiring effort.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stroke of genius' is a set phrase, but it must be split: the definition is only 'Stroke', a gentle touch.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stroking a cat or a cheek is a gentle, loving touch.

entries.clue: Endured pain in the neck (4)

blocks.note: the past tense of bear, to put up with
an idiom for a tiresome, tedious person

annotation.surface: Someone put up with a sore neck.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'pain in the neck' a literal ache; it is the idiom for an annoying person.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the past of bear (she bore it well) and a tedious person who wears you out.

entries.clue: Protocol later allows outside security (10)

indicatorNotes.outside: the answer is built from the outside edges of the words around it: the tail of one word, all of the next, and the head of the third

annotation.surface: A rule that permits external safeguarding at a later stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Protocol' sounds formal enough to be a definition, but it just carries three letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A banking sense: property pledged against a loan is the lender's security if the borrower defaults.

entries.clue: Truth with nothing replacing electronic hunger (8)

indicatorNotes.replacing: one thing replacing another takes its place, so O stands where E stood

blocks.note: O = zero, nothing; it comes in
E = electronic, as in e-mail; it goes out

annotation.surface: Honesty that swaps nothing in for a craving for gadgets.
annotation.walkthrough: One letter changes and truth turns into greed; 'electronic hunger' is a false phrase to be split.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a voracious eater has a huge appetite, and the noun is that ravenous hunger.

entries.clue: Ocean floor beginning to swallow sailor (6)

indicatorNotes.to swallow: what is swallowed goes inside, so the first word takes the second into its middle

blocks.note: a seed is the beginning from which something grows

annotation.surface: The bottom of the sea starts to engulf a mariner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beginning' looks like a first-letter instruction, but it is a whole word that opens to take the sailor.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the bottom of the sea, compound of sea and bed.

entries.clue: Covering sweetheart in fond embrace (9)

indicatorNotes.in: one piece sits in the other
indicatorNotes.embrace: an embrace wraps arms around someone, so the outer word wraps the inner one

blocks.note: pet as a term of endearment

annotation.surface: Lovers wrapped in a tender hug.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole romantic scene hides a floor covering.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: fitted carpet is one kind of floor covering.

entries.clue: Grind edges of green residue (5)

indicatorNotes.edges of: the edges of a word are its two outer letters, first and last

blocks.note: ash is what remains after burning

annotation.surface: Milling the rims of some green leftovers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grind' could be mill or toil; here it is what teeth do in anger.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for teeth: to grind them together in rage is to gnash them.

entries.clue: Study missing one old head teacher (9)

indicatorNotes.missing: a word missing something has lost it, so the named letter is left out

blocks.note: study = GO OVER, which drops one of its two Os (O = old)
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Inverness

annotation.surface: A former head teacher, going over her studies, finds one missing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old head teacher' reads as a phrase; split it: 'old' goes with the deletion and 'head' is a headland.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a woman employed to teach children in their own home is one kind of teacher.

entries.clue: Protocol holds attention, ready for danger (7)

indicatorNotes.holds: a container holds its contents inside, so the outer word holds the inner

blocks.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

annotation.surface: Official procedure keeps people alert and prepared for trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is a verb here: the definition means to prepare someone for danger.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom's verb: 'forewarned is forearmed', to arm in advance, so to make ready for danger.

entries.clue: Lift English tax, in part raised (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the first pieces go inside the last
indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raising a word lifts its bottom letter to the top, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: a part in a play is a role

annotation.surface: A demand to abolish an English tax, partly brought in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lift' looks like a verb meaning cancel the tax; it is the noun, the thing in a building.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: the US word for what the British call a lift.

entries.clue: Cross about dull tool? (7)

indicatorNotes.about: turned about, as a soldier turns to face the other way, so read backwards

blocks.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix

annotation.surface: Someone is angry about a blunt implement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry but is the noun. The question mark flags the definition as figurative.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: someone who lets everyone walk over them is a doormat, and a person others use is their tool.

entries.clue: Loving installing new decking (8)

indicatorNotes.installing: what is installed is put in place inside, so the outer word takes the letter in

annotation.surface: A fond builder putting in a new deck.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Decking' looks like the timber platform; it is the verb deck, to decorate.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: decking a hall with holly is decorating it.

entries.clue: A noise around tenant’s top floor (7)

indicatorNotes.around: one word goes around the other, enclosing it
indicatorNotes.top: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the A stays as it is

annotation.surface: A racket from the flat upstairs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Floor' looks like part of the building, reinforced by 'tenant' and 'top'; it is a verb, to stun.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: news that floors you knocks you flat with surprise.

entries.clue: One’s tossed about, about bowled over (5)

annotation.definitionNote: 'One's tossed' means one that is tossed

indicatorNotes.over: turned over, so flipped end to end and read backwards

blocks.note: b = bowled on a cricket scorecard

annotation.surface: Someone is thrown around, knocked flat.
annotation.walkthrough: The two 'about's do different jobs, one Latin and one from memo headings. The Highland games are Scottish athletics meetings.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the tree trunk heaved end over end at Highland games is the thing tossed.

entries.clue: Americans were partially providing solution (6)

indicatorNotes.partially: what appears partially shows only a part of itself, so the letters needed hide inside the words

annotation.surface: Americans were in part responsible for solving the problem.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Partially' reads as 'in part responsible'; it is the hiding instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the solution to a puzzle or a problem is its answer.

entries.clue: Slur like individual imbibing Asti, lastly (9)

indicatorNotes.imbibing: to imbibe is to drink in, so the drink ends up inside
indicatorNotes.lastly: what comes lastly comes at the end, so take the word's final letter

annotation.surface: A drinker of sparkling Italian wine slurs their words.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slur' in a drinking scene suggests drunken speech; it means an insult. Asti is an Italian sparkling wine.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to cast aspersions is to make damaging remarks, slurs on someone's character.

entries.clue: Sun‘s opening with buxom specimen (6)

indicatorNotes.opening: a word's opening is where it begins, its first letter

annotation.surface: A tabloid's page three, the Sun opening with a curvy model.
annotation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper once known for its topless page-three models, which is the picture here.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a specimen taken for testing, like blood or soil, is a sample.

entries.clue: Rule empire including great nation, initially (5)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so each word gives its initial

blocks.note: first letters of Rule Empire Including Great Nation

annotation.surface: Governing an empire that includes a great country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rule' is both the definition and the first word of the acrostic, and the whole clue describes what a monarch's rule is.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a monarch's reign is the period and fact of their rule over an empire.

entries.clue: Grounds of divorce’s end, say (6)

indicatorNotes.end: a word's end is its last letter

annotation.surface: The reasons given for a marriage ending.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grounds of divorce' is a legal phrase; here 'Grounds' is land, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a country house's grounds, its land and gardens, are its estate.

entries.clue: Deck hands inside almost busy (8)

indicatorNotes.inside: one piece goes inside the other
indicatorNotes.almost: almost the whole word is not quite all of it, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: busy = ornate, over-decorated; almost drops the final E

annotation.surface: Crew below deck, nearly flat out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deck' and 'hands' make a ship; Deck is a verb, to decorate.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to deck the halls is to decorate them with trimmings.

entries.clue: Things within people note in diary (10)

indicatorNotes.within: a thing within another sits inside it
indicatorNotes.in: one letter goes in the word

blocks.note: a log is a daily record

annotation.surface: Personal notes jotted in a journal about what's inside people.
annotation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the note goes into the diary first, and that result goes into the people.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: your things, as in 'pack your things', are your personal possessions.

entries.clue: Provided fast time (4)

blocks.note: the Christian season of fasting before Easter

annotation.surface: Someone supplied a quick moment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fast' reads as quick; it is fasting.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the past of lend, and the forty days of Christian fasting before Easter.
